# Job Chapter 37 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 430r–430v

---

**1** At this also my heart trembles and leaps from its place. **2** Hear, hear the thunder of his voice and the rumbling that comes from his mouth!

**3** Under the whole heaven he lets it loose, and his lightning to the corners of the earth. **4** After it his voice roars; he thunders with the voice of his majesty, and he does not restrain them when his voice is heard.

**5** God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things that we cannot comprehend. **6** For to the snow he says, 'Fall on the earth,' and to the downpour, his mighty downpour of rain.

**7** He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it. **8** Then the beasts go into their lairs and remain in their dens.

**9** From its chamber comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds. **10** By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen. **11** He loads the thick cloud with moisture; the clouds scatter his lightning. **12** They turn round and round by his guidance, to accomplish all that he commands them on the face of the inhabited world — **13** whether for correction, or for his land, or for covenant-faithfulness, he causes it to happen.

**14** Hear this, O Job; stop and consider the wondrous works of God. **15** Do you know how God lays his command upon them and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine? **16** Do you know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?

**17** You whose garments are hot when the earth is still because of the south wind — **18** can you, like him, spread out the skies, hard as a cast metal mirror?

**19** Teach us what we shall say to him; we cannot draw up our case because of darkness. **20** Shall it be told him that I wish to speak? Did a man ever wish that he would be swallowed up?

**21** And now men cannot look at the light when it is bright in the skies, when the wind has passed and cleared them. **22** Out of the north comes golden splendor; God is clothed with fearsome majesty.

**23** The Almighty — we cannot find him; he is great in power and justice and abundant righteousness; he does not oppress. **24** Therefore men fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own conceit."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verses 1-5 — Thunder as divine speech:** Elihu treats the thunderstorm as a direct manifestation of God's voice. The Hebrew word *qol* (voice) applies equally to thunder and speech — the storm is not merely a metaphor for God's power but an actual form of divine communication.

**Verse 13 — Three purposes of weather:** The storm comes for correction (*shevet*, rod), for the land, or for *chesed* (covenant-faithfulness/steadfast love). This tripartite scheme is Elihu's most sophisticated theology of providence: not all divine acts are punitive; some are provision, some are love.

**Verses 21-24 — The hinge to theophany:** Elihu's final words describe golden splendor breaking through clearing skies from the north and God "clothed with fearsome majesty." His speech ends with awe, not argument. This is the transition — the next voice to speak will be God's own, from the whirlwind.

*— LOGOS*
